goal: Improve Qwen3.8-27B on blackbox web-security tasks using only Fleet cyber training tasks.
scope: The rankings are informed starting points, not measured winners. Each comparison should change only the settings named by its shaded cells. The 20-task development set is used to choose settings. The 10-task final Fleet set stays untouched until finalists are chosen. WebExploitBench is run after accepted training runs as development evidence and cannot also be described as an untouched final test.

runs.research_question: Can balanced strong-teacher actions improve unseen Fleet tasks?
runs.why_priority: Strong simple baseline; fixes the old five-window sampling weakness.
runs.launch_after: New data audit and one-step check pass

runs.research_question: Does Qwen learn better from its own successful style?
runs.why_priority: Directly tests style matching at the same training dose.

runs.research_question: Does an equal teacher-and-Qwen mixture combine strategy quality with style matching?
runs.why_priority: A mixed source is a plausible winner and connects the first two results.
runs.launch_after: Matched teacher and self token pools exist

changes.source_balance: Equal teacher and Qwen target tokens

runs.research_question: Does removing navigation-only behavior concentrate learning on useful problem solving?
runs.why_priority: Extraction may matter more than small optimizer changes.
runs.launch_after: Action labels pass a blinded spot check

changes.target_actions: Exploration, exploit-changing, recovery, and report actions
changes.windows_per_trace: One example per distinct useful action

runs.research_question: Does the main teacher result repeat on a second balanced split?
runs.why_priority: Protects against a lucky development assignment.

runs.research_question: Is learning rate 1e-6 too cautious?
runs.why_priority: 3e-6 is an informative high boundary.

runs.research_question: Is learning rate 1e-6 too aggressive?
runs.why_priority: 3e-7 tests the stable low boundary.

runs.research_question: Do noisier, more frequent updates generalize better?
runs.why_priority: Batch 8 is the small useful boundary.

runs.research_question: Do smoother, larger updates improve stability?
runs.why_priority: Batch 64 explores the opposite boundary.

runs.research_question: Is one pass too little for sparse successful records?
runs.why_priority: Two passes are the smallest meaningful dose increase.
runs.launch_after: Stable learning rate and batch are selected

runs.research_question: Does substantially more repetition help or overfit?
runs.why_priority: Four passes reveal the high-dose boundary.

runs.research_question: Does a teacher-heavy mixture beat 50:50?
runs.why_priority: Refines the mix toward stronger strategy demonstrations.
runs.launch_after: SFT-03 matches or beats both single sources

runs.research_question: Does a Qwen-heavy mixture beat 50:50?
runs.why_priority: Tests whether style matching matters more than teacher coverage.
runs.launch_after: SFT-03 matches or beats both single sources

runs.research_question: Do shorter examples give cleaner local learning signals?
runs.why_priority: 8K may reduce unrelated context.
runs.launch_after: Data source and optimizer range are selected

runs.research_question: Does more context teach multi-step exploit chains better?
runs.why_priority: 32K may help long chains but costs more and can dilute the signal.

runs.research_question: Should exploration and exploit-changing actions count twice as much as reporting?
runs.why_priority: Tests whether easy final wording gets too much loss weight.
runs.compare_with: Same recipe with equal stage weights

runs.research_question: Would a three-times smaller update be more stable?
runs.why_priority: RL is sensitive to update size; this is the first safer boundary.

runs.research_question: Does a very small update avoid drift or under-train?
runs.why_priority: Explores the low boundary after the more likely 3e-7.

runs.research_question: Can a larger update learn faster without collapse?
runs.why_priority: Informative but more likely to destabilize full-weight 27B training.

runs.research_question: Do more attempts per task improve advantage estimates?
runs.why_priority: Cleaner within-task comparison at twice the generation cost.
runs.launch_after: Stable actor learning rate is selected

runs.research_question: Does more task variety beat more attempts per task?
runs.why_priority: Uses the same 64 attempts as RL-11 across twice as many tasks.
runs.launch_after: RL-11 cost and signal are measured

runs.research_question: Is the stay-close penalty blocking useful movement?
runs.why_priority: Strong interpretable boundary, with drift risk.

runs.research_question: Would a ten-times stronger stay-close penalty help?

runs.research_question: Do larger upward than downward updates help rare successes?

runs.research_question: Do less-random attempts produce more usable rewards?
runs.why_priority: May raise success rate but reduce strategy diversity.

runs.research_question: Do more-random attempts discover more strategies?
runs.why_priority: Explores the opposite boundary but may waste attempts.
runs.launch_after: RL-16 gives a clean low-temperature comparison

runs.research_question: Does removing the lowest-probability token tail help?
runs.why_priority: Standard practical boundary, but overlaps with temperature.

runs.research_question: Does equal application sampling improve transfer?
runs.why_priority: Prevents the largest application from dominating updates.
runs.launch_after: Task metadata and reward rates are complete
